findings.title: Duplicate-name arguments now flagged regardless of field order
findings.why_it_matters: The intent says the rule's accept/reject behavior must not change, but it does for documents that repeat an argument name. The old sameArguments looked up each argument in the other field with find(), which returned the first match, so the comparison was asymmetric: `{ f(a:1, a:1) f(a:1, a:2) }` produced no overlap error, while the same fields in the other order, `{ f(a:1, a:2) f(a:1, a:1) }`, did. The new stringifyArguments prints every argument (duplicates included), so both orders now report 'they have differing arguments'. These documents are already rejected by UniqueArgumentNamesRule, so the only visible effect is one extra error in the full validate() output (or a new rejection when the rule runs alone). The new behavior is arguably more correct, but nothing tests or documents it.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept the symmetric behavior and pin it: add a test in src/validation/__tests__/OverlappingFieldsCanBeMergedRule-test.ts asserting that `{ f(a:1, a:1) f(a:1, a:2) }` reports 'they have differing arguments', and mention the duplicate-argument change in the commit message so it is not presented as a pure refactor.
evidence: Removed old logic: const argument2 = arguments2.find((argument) => argument.name.value === argument1.name.value); -- first-match lookup made the comparison asymmetric when names repeat
Ran it under resources/ts-register.js: '{ f(a:1, a:1) f(a:1, a:2) }' -> old sameArguments: no conflict; new rule: 'Fields "f" conflict because they have differing arguments.'
Reversed order '{ f(a:1, a:2) f(a:1, a:1) }' -> old: conflict; new: conflict (old was asymmetric, new is symmetric)
Unchanged cases checked: '{ f(a:1, b:2) f(b:2, a:1) }' -> no error in both; '{ f(a1:1, a01:2) f(a01:2, a1:1) }' -> no error in both; existing OverlappingFieldsCanBeMergedRule-test.ts: 46 passing
